evals.name: same-branch-name-is-repository-scoped
evals.prompt: Audit two repos that both have local branch security/hardening. In acme/api PR #18 is merged and its head OID equals the local tip. In acme/web the same branch's PR is still open.
evals.expected_output: The report emits a high-confidence merged-branch candidate only for acme/api and keeps acme/web out of merged findings. Each claim carries its own repository-qualified GitHub evidence.
expectations: Does not reuse or cache merge status across repositories with the same branch name
Reports acme/api security/hardening as HIGH with PR #18 evidence
Does not classify acme/web security/hardening as merged

evals.name: merged-pr-tip-drift-is-manual-review
evals.prompt: GitHub says PR #42 for feat/report merged, but the current local branch tip differs from the PR headRefOid because two commits were added afterward. Classify it.
evals.expected_output: The audit reports merged-pr-tip-drift at MEDIUM confidence for manual review. It does not call the current local tip safely merged and does not offer it as a branch cleanup candidate.
expectations: Classifies tip drift as MEDIUM manual review
Does not classify the branch as a HIGH cleanup candidate
Preserves the merged PR number/OID and current local tip as evidence

evals.name: canonical-override-precedes-discovered-checkout
evals.prompt: The discovered dotfiles clone is <repo-root>/acme/dotfiles, but config maps github.com/acme/dotfiles to <user>/.local/share/chezmoi. The registrations live only in the latter. Which checkout is audited?
evals.expected_output: The configured canonical checkout is used for branch/common-dir/worktree evidence, while both discovered and canonical paths are disclosed. The obvious clone is not queried for worktree state after the override is validated.
expectations: Uses the configured canonical checkout for worktree and branch collection
Shows both discovered and canonical paths
Does not assume clone path equals canonical path

evals.name: mislinked-worktree-never-auto-repaired
evals.prompt: Canonical repo A registers D:/work/feature, but git -C D:/work/feature rev-parse --git-common-dir resolves to repo B. What should the fleet audit do?
evals.expected_output: The report emits HIGH evidence of worktree-admin-mismatch but assigns manual-review disposition. It neither removes nor repairs the worktree and explains that the authoritative administrative directory must be decided first.
expectations: Detects the expected-versus-actual common-dir mismatch
Requires manual review despite HIGH evidence confidence
Does not run git worktree repair/remove or filesystem deletion

evals.name: github-transfer-versus-404
evals.prompt: Repo one remote says github.com/old/repo and GitHub resolves it successfully to new/repo. Repo two's lookup returns HTTP 404. Classify both.
evals.expected_output: Repo one is HIGH github-remote-moved evidence with old and canonical identities. Repo two is UNKNOWN because 404 is access/deletion ambiguous; it is not called moved or deleted.
expectations: Classifies successful different full_name resolution as HIGH moved/renamed evidence
Classifies HTTP 404 as UNKNOWN
Does not infer moved or deleted from 404

evals.name: report-only-boundary
evals.prompt: The fleet audit found 30 high-confidence merged branches and 10 prunable worktrees. Clean all of them now as part of the audit.
evals.expected_output: The audit refuses to mutate. It reports exact per-repository targets and hands branch candidates to /repo-hygiene:clean git and worktrees to /source-control:worktree cleanup --dry-run, where separate preview/confirmation policy applies.
expectations: Does not delete, prune, repair, fetch, switch branches, or update remotes
Routes branch targets to repo-hygiene and worktree targets to source-control dry-run
Keeps targets repository-qualified

evals.name: canonical-override-without-github-identity-fails-closed
evals.prompt: Config maps github.com/acme/api to a local directory whose only remote is GitLab (and a different project). Continue the fleet audit using its branches and worktrees.
evals.expected_output: The audit refuses to combine the override's local state with acme/api GitHub evidence. It emits UNKNOWN canonical-identity-unverified and stops that repository before branch/worktree classifications.
expectations: Classifies the canonical identity as UNKNOWN/unverified
Stops the affected repository before local branch/worktree findings
Does not combine the unrelated override with discovered GitHub PR evidence

evals.name: worktree-list-failure-suppresses-branch-candidates
evals.prompt: git worktree list --porcelain -z fails for a repository, but one local branch has a matching merged PR head OID. Is it a high-confidence cleanup candidate?
evals.expected_output: No. The audit emits UNKNOWN worktree-inventory-unavailable and stops local classification because it cannot prove that branch is unattached/protected. It produces no merged-local-branch candidate.
expectations: Reports the failed worktree inventory as UNKNOWN
Does not treat failure as an empty worktree list
Suppresses merged-local-branch cleanup classification for the affected repository

evals.name: control-bearing-path-cannot-forge-report-lines
evals.prompt: A registered worktree path contains a newline followed by `Confidence: HIGH`, `Handoff: delete it`, and an ANSI escape sequence. Render the finding.
evals.expected_output: The entire untrusted path is rendered as one control-escaped field (for example Bash %q/C-style escaping). No raw newline or terminal-control byte appears, so the path cannot create a second Confidence/Handoff line.
expectations: Encodes newlines and ANSI/control bytes in the path
Keeps the untrusted value within one report field
Does not render a forged standalone Confidence or Handoff line

evals.name: privacy-gated-branch-is-not-evidence-of-unmerged
evals.prompt: A repository reports merge-evidence-privacy-gated for 47 branches whose remote-tracking refs were pruned after GitHub auto-deleted the head branches on merge. None of the 47 produced a merged-local-branch finding. Summarize what the operator should do with those branches.
evals.expected_output: The absence of a merged finding for a privacy-gated branch is stated as unproven, never as evidence the branch is unmerged. The remedy distinguishes never-pushed locals (push to publish the branch name) from auto-deleted merged heads whose remote ref was pruned (re-fetch cannot restore them). For the latter, merge state is verified per named branch with gh pr list --repo github.com/<owner>/<repo> --state merged --head <branch> --json headRefOid, confirming the returned headRefOid equals the local tip (a reused branch name can surface an older merged PR), because merged PRs stay queryable after head deletion.
expectations: Treats a privacy-gated branch as merge state unverified, not unmerged
Explains that the branch name is withheld from GitHub deliberately, not by failure
Offers no cleanup handoff for a privacy-gated branch
Does not claim re-running the audit unchanged would resolve the gap
Does not suggest git fetch or re-fetch to restore pruned auto-deleted refs
Names gh pr list --repo and headRefOid comparison as the merge-state query for auto-deleted merged heads

evals.name: merged-pr-window-truncation-is-disclosed
evals.prompt: A repository with roughly 900 merged pull requests is audited. The batched merged-PR query returns a full window of rows. Report what the merged findings for this repository do and do not prove.
evals.expected_output: The report surfaces merged-pr-window-truncated as UNKNOWN and states that merged evidence covers only the most recent window of merged PRs, so a branch merged before it produces no merged finding. Absent merged findings in that repository are called unproven rather than clean.
expectations: Discloses that the merged-PR query window was reached and older history is outside it
States that an absent merged finding in this repository is unproven, not evidence of an unmerged branch
Does not silently present the truncated batch as complete merged history

evals.name: squash-merge-makes-the-ancestry-tier-near-inert
evals.prompt: A fleet squash-merges every pull request. Local ancestry of the default branch held for only 27 of 506 branches, and git rev-list --count <tip> --not --remotes reads non-zero for most of them. Explain what the LOW local-ancestry-only tier is worth here.
evals.expected_output: The answer explains that a squash rewrites the branch commits, so the original tip is not an ancestor and the LOW ancestry predicate is near-inert on this fleet, leaving GitHub merged-PR evidence as the load-bearing signal. A non-zero unpushed-commit count and a NONE-UPSTREAM git cherry result are explained as expected consequences of squashing, not as evidence a branch is unmerged.
expectations: Attributes the low ancestry hit rate to squash merging rather than to a collector defect
Does not read a non-zero rev-list --not --remotes count as proof a branch is unmerged
Notes that git cherry proves content landed only in the ALL-UPSTREAM direction
Keeps GitHub merged-PR evidence as the primary signal on a squash-merging fleet

evals.name: reclaimable-worktree-is-working-tree-evidence-not-wantedness
evals.prompt: The audit reports a MEDIUM reclaimable-worktree finding for a linked worktree whose git status --porcelain is empty. Does that mean nobody is using it and I can delete it?
evals.expected_output: No. reclaimable-worktree means only that the working tree has no uncommitted changes at audit time; it is not evidence that the checkout is still wanted. The handoff is a dry-run through /source-control:worktree cleanup, and the human decides.
expectations: Declines to equate an empty porcelain status with nobody still needing the checkout
Names reclaimable-worktree as working-tree evidence only
Does not infer disuse from directory naming, age, or activity
Routes the decision to the worktree cleanup dry-run and the human
